sense: a part of the school year

terms.gloss: a term at school or university
terms.comment: A plain description from classical words: spatium is a stretch of time (spatium temporis).

evidence: M-O s.v. semester (academic), citing Gauss and Mosellanus’s Paedologia
terms.comment: The neuter of sēmestris, lasting six months (Cic. Att. 10.8.7; Caes. BC 1.9, Lewis & Short).

semestre.html: Lewis & Short marks only the first e (sēmestris, from sex and mēnsis); Traupman prints semestre on p. 376 and sēmēstre on p. 392. The length of the second vowel is not settled here.

sources: Lewis & Short: studium · Lewis & Short: spatium · Lewis & Short: semestris
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 376, 392, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. semester (academic).
